_doc.purpose: Maps detector coder-IDs to plain-English pattern names + family + description for use in user-facing memory ('you understand X', 'you missed Y again'). Authored 2026-05-23 by Claude as v1 starters per Mohit's P1; voice tuning expected once he reviews in the UI.
_doc.audience: 600-1500 rated players — no jargon (no 'fianchetto', 'prophylaxis', 'zwischenzug'). Name the square / the idea instead.

schema.pattern_id: Stable snake_case key. Used in user_pattern_events docs as the pattern reference. NEVER renamed once shipped — only the human_name/description/family fields are tunable.
schema.human_name: Short coach-voice name, 3-6 words. What you'd say to a student.
schema.short_description: One sentence in coach voice. WHY it matters or WHAT it does, not just what it is.
schema.family: Tactical/positional grouping. Used to roll up related patterns in insights ('you handle the Légal's family well — 4/5 hits').
schema.example_fen: Canonical example position. Optional — null means Mohit will fill from a known game later.

missed_mate.short_description: There was a forced mating sequence — every opponent reply loses.

missed_piece.short_description: A clean way to win a knight, bishop, rook, or queen — the engine saw it cleanly.

clearance_for_attack.human_name: Open the line so your piece attacks
clearance_for_attack.short_description: Move a piece out of the way so another of yours has a direct shot at the king or a key square.

clearance_then_check.short_description: Sacrifice a knight (or pawn) to open the line so your queen can deliver check on the next move.

queen_fork_capture_with_check.short_description: Queen move that grabs material and checks the king on the same turn.

queen_fork.short_description: Queen move that attacks the king and another loose piece at once.

attack_with_tempo.short_description: Hit an enemy piece with a move that also improves yours — opponent has to react.

endgame_loose_pawn_capture.short_description: In the endgame, your active piece grabs an opponent pawn that has no defender.

endgame_loose_pawn_attack.short_description: In the endgame, move an active piece next to an opponent pawn that has no defender — you can grab it next.

un_developing.short_description: Moving a developed piece back to its starting square wastes a tempo — usually a better move exists.

defensive_pawn_push.human_name: Don't push wing pawns when you should be developing
defensive_pawn_push.short_description: Slow wing pawn moves (a3, h6) cost time when the position is asking for a piece to come out.

knight_outpost.human_name: Knight to a defended central square
knight_outpost.short_description: Park a knight on a central square that's protected by your own pawn and can't be kicked away — a long-term home.

stop_opp_pawn.human_name: Block opponent's pawn before it pushes
stop_opp_pawn.short_description: Get a piece or pawn in front of opponent's pawn so they can't keep pushing it into your camp.

active_defense.short_description: A move that protects your threatened piece AND hits something of theirs — turns defense into pressure.

same_piece_better_square.short_description: Same piece type you moved, but to a square where it hits more loose targets at once.

discovered_vacating_check.human_name: Move gives check; vacated square opens attack
discovered_vacating_check.short_description: Move a piece to check the king while the square it leaves opens a line for another of yours to hit a loose target.

knight_on_rim.human_name: Avoid knight on the rim in the opening
knight_on_rim.short_description: Knights on the a- or h-file in the opening attack very few squares — develop toward the center instead.

pawn_kicks_piece.human_name: Pawn push that kicks an enemy piece
pawn_kicks_piece.short_description: Pawn move that attacks an enemy piece, forcing it to retreat — gains time.

blocked_own_pawn.short_description: A piece move that sits where your own pawn needed to advance — usually push the pawn first.

king_pawn_lifted.human_name: Attack the weak square in front of the king
king_pawn_lifted.short_description: Opponent's f- or g-pawn moved off its starting square, leaving a weak point in front of the king — pile up there.

trap_punishment.short_description: Opponent reached a setup that's part of a known trap; the engine's move is the textbook refutation.
